subject: Offer approval: L4 Platform Engineer — base/bonus/equity proposal
messages:

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Offer approval request — L4 Platform Engineer (Ryan Choe)

Team,

Following our final loop with Ryan (attached resume), I'm proposing the following standard L4 package for approval so we can get an offer out this week:

- Base: $170,000/year
- Target bonus: 10% (annual, discretionary)
- Equity: 0.50% RSU grant, 4-year vesting, 1-year cliff
- Sign-on: $0 proposed (open to 1x discretionary if needed)
- Headcount: conversion from open HC in Q3 hiring plan (HRREQ-4321)

Attached: compensation calculation workbook with modeled ramp & total comp. This candidate comes from a competing infra startup; market comps attached for reference. Can comp committee confirm in principle and flag any concerns on budget or structure?

If we want to be competitive we could shift to $175k base or include a $10k sign-on. I prefer keeping base conservative and using a sign-on if necessary.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Markus —

Thanks for the summary and for looping HR. A couple quick clarifying items before comp committee sign-off:

1) Candidate preference: Ryan indicated he'd prefer a slightly higher base over sign-on, but is flexible.
2) Relocation: He is remote but willing to relocate if needed — no relocation stipend requested today.
3) Notice period: 3 weeks, earliest start ~ 2027-06-15.

I also attached the latest market benchmark we used for similar Platform roles (April 2027). If we decide on a $175k base, I recommend keeping the RSU at 0.5% and waiving sign-on. If we keep $170k, consider a $7.5k–$10k sign-on to close.

Let me know which direction you want me to present to the candidate.

—Marissa

3) Keep base and sign-on as proposed, increase equity to 0.60% (ask Eng L4 band lead).

Team —

I reviewed the headcount and the modeled run-rate. We have bench HC clearance for Q3 (HRREQ-4321) and can absorb the recurring spend within the hiring plan, but two notes from finance:

1) Prefer conservative base given current FY27 cash plan. Recommend option 2 (keep base at $170k) paired with a $10k one-time sign-on paid after start + standard 12% bonus target (slightly increase from proposed 10%). That keeps total first-year on-target comp competitive while limiting recurring base impact.

2) If we increase base to $175k, finance will require a headcount reforecast for FY27 and sign-off from FP&A (slows offer by ~3 business days).

If hiring agrees, finance approves option 2 now. I attached a headcount-impact extract.

Laura Bennett
